citation: Chicago Public Library, "Technology That Changed Chicago: Gaslight", Chicago Public Library blog
author: Chicago Public Library
locator: the post's account of the gas era: the first gaslights of 4 September 1850, mantles in the 1890s, gas streetlights still used in some areas into the early 1900s, electric light common by 1909
rights_note: A library's blog post; cite the text, derive no asset.
access_notes: Read on 2026-11-03 for T-3334 over plain HTTPS.
what_it_supplies: THE CITY STILL LIT SOME STREETS BY GAS in the early 1900s: the city, which regulated Peoples Gas, 'still used gas streetlights in some areas'.

GAS MANTLES from the 1890s: 'Gas mantles, producing brighter light with only one-twelfth the gas consumption, became available in the 1890s', so a gas lamp of 1904 can burn a mantle's whiter light rather than an open flame's.
ELECTRIC LIGHT ARRIVING: 'Electric lights were common by 1909'.
what_it_does_not_supply: which streets were lit by gas and which by electricity in 1904, or Prairie Avenue's in particular
how many lamps, their hours, or who lit them
whether any Prairie Avenue house was lit by gas, by electricity or by both
note: Written for T-3334 (1904 by night). A general account of the city's gaslight, not a record of this district: it supports drawing the district's lamp posts (L-prairie-street-lamps-3199) lit as gas lamps with mantles, and a mix of gas and electric light in the houses, and nothing more particular.
